It proceeds to investigate institutional context and processes relevant to policy making, using case studies. With this foundation, the course explores specific policy problems and solutions related to important problem areas such as economic growth, health care, monetary policy, education, and environment. Students will be encouraged to investigate policy areas of interest for case studies and papers. Prerequisites: Economics 111 or Political Science 101 and second-year standing. STAFF

system_requisites: Second-year standing - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: Environmental Law & Policy. Also listed as ENV-295. This course examines how societies govern environmental challenges through the lens of law, policy, and political institutions. Students trace the evolution of environmental governance-from early conservation to modern regulation-exploring the constitutional foundations of administrative authority, property rights, and federalism. The curriculum focuses on the implementation and evaluation of major statutes-such as the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and NEPA-while introducing key economic concepts like externalities, market-based instruments, and environmental justice. By analyzing the trade-offs between economic development and ecological protection, students will learn to assess legitimacy and effectiveness of regulatory frameworks. Through critical engagement with legal and scholarly texts, students will develop the skills to communicate evidence-based arguments regarding contemporary environmental crises. Prerequisite: Second-year standing.

system_requisites: PST-320 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: In this course students will use the techniques of policy analysis they studied in PST-320 to conduct an independent research project. Normally these projects will be related to the student's major or other curricular interest. During the first several course meetings students will identify and refine their policy area for in-depth study. This course will meet once per week during the spring semester, and will culminate with individual presentations of the policy research. Prerequisite: Policy Studies 320. STAFF.

system_requisites: None
course_description: An introduction to principles of psychological science and inquiry. Major topics of psychology are covered with consideration of different approaches psychologists take to describe, predict, and explain behavior. Emphasis is placed on theory, research, and application. Laboratory work is required. Prerequisite: none. STAFF.

system_requisites: None
course_description: Introductory Special Topic: Fundamentals of Statistics in Psychology. An introduction to quantitative analysis necessary for understanding and creating knowledge in psychology. Students will become knowledgable concerning the use of common statistics for description, correlation, and infrerence. Students will analyze data for supporting or critiquing research arguments. Prerequisite: None.

description_prerequisite: Psychology 113 and Mathematics/Social Studies 115, or Statistics 209
system_requisites: PSY-113 and SST-115, MAT-115, STA-209 or PSY-195, ST: Statistics in Psychology - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course describes experimental designs and attendant statistical techniques. Students learn to use quantitative methods to pose meaningful questions to data. Topics include between-group and within-group designs, analysis of variance for main effects and interactions, the adaptation of statistical inquiry to less than optimal situations, and critical thinking about research methods. Prerequisite: Psychology 113 and Mathematics/Social Studies 115, or Statistics 209. STAFF.

description_prerequisite: Psychology 113 and current enrollment in or previous completion of: and Mathematics/Social Studies 115, or Statistics 209
system_requisites: PSY-113 and MAT-115, SST-115, or STA 209 - Must be completed prior to taking this course. previous completion of or current registration in MAT/SST 115 or STA 209 - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.
course_description: This course explores psychological development from the prenatal period through adolescence. Major theoretical perspectives on the nature of developmental change are considered with a focus on empirical reseach and application of each perspective. Topics include physical, cognitive, emotional, and social development. Laboratory work is required. Prerequisite: Psychology 113 and current enrollment in or previous completion of: and Mathematics/Social Studies 115, or Statistics 209. ELLIS.

description_prerequisite: Psychology 113, and Mathematics/Social Studies 115, or Statistics 209
system_requisites: PSY-113 and MAT-115, SST-115, or STA 209 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: The course studies behavior as it occurs in its environmental context. Topics in learning and motivation are analyzed through the experimental approach of behavior analytic psychology. Topics include classical and operant learning, choice, self-control, and extrinsic and intrinsic motivation. Laboratory work is required. Prerequisite: Psychology 113, and Mathematics/Social Studies 115, or Statistics 209. LOPATTO.

system_requisites: PSY-113. MAT/SST-115, or STA 209 is recommended - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: The study of psychopathology. Framed around the National Institute of Mental Health's Research Domain Criteria, emphasis is given to experimental models and the interactions among psychological, neurobiological, social, and environmental processes that inform mental disorder. Some attention is given to treatments and the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders." Prerequisite: Psychology 113. Mathematics/Social Studies 115, or Statistics 209 recommended. RALSTON.

description_prerequisite: PSY-113 and completion of or current enrollment in SST-115, STA-209, or PSY-195 Fundamentals of Statistics in Psychology
system_requisites: PSY-113 and concurrent enrollment in or pevious completion of SST-115, STA-209, or PSY-195 Fundamentals of Statistics in Psychology - Must be completed prior to taking this course. SST-115, STA-209 or PSY-195 - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.
course_description: Human beings are a cultural species, endlessly shaped by the unique social contexts and environments in which we are enmeshed.  How can culture be defined, and what are the dimensions of culture?  What psychological and cognitive processes, previously thought to be universal, actually vary dynamically by culture?  How does culture influence self-concept, emotion, attention, memory, and health?  What methodological issues arise when studying culture and cultural processes? Laboratory work may be required. Prerequisite: PSY-113 and completion of or current enrollment in SST-115, STA-209, or PSY-195 Fundamentals of Statistics in Psychology.

description_prerequisite: Psychology 225 and 233 and one additional psychology course numbered 200 or above
system_requisites: PSY-225, PSY-233 and one additional psychology course numbered 200 or above - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: An advanced investigation of substantive topics in developmental psychology. Emphasis is placed on theory and research. Laboratory work may be required. Prerequisite: Psychology 225 and 233 and one additional psychology course numbered 200 or above. ELLIS.

description_prerequisite: Psychology 225 and two Psychology courses numbered 200 or above
system_requisites: PSY-225 and two psychology courses numbered 200 or above - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Students will learn about methods of test development, the statistical analysis of test data, and social implications of testing. In lab, students will develop testing instruments and learn multivariate data analysis. Topics covered include intelligence and personality testing, systems of behavioral observation, regression, factor analysis, and theories of test construction. Prerequisite: Psychology 225 and two Psychology courses numbered 200 or above. RALSTON.

system_requisites: PSY-246 or NRS-250 and PSY 225 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Students in this course will examine how changes in the brain, in conjunction with cognitive and behavioral processes, result from the interactions between an organism and the environment throughout the life span. Topics will include neural and functional consequences of environmental deprivation or enrichment, sensory system plasticity, language learning, recovery from stroke, and cognitive enhancement. Prerequisite: PSY-246 or NRS-250 and PSY-225. REMPEL-CLOWER

description_prerequisite: PSY-225 and two additional 200 level psychology courses
system_requisites: PSY 225 and two additional 200 level psychology courses - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Advanced Special Topic: Introduction to Meta-Analysis in Psychology. This course introduces the use of meta-analyses in psychology. Students will learn the key ideas and theory that underlie meta-analysis and will learn how to use statistical software to to synthesize research across studies. Laboratory work is required. Prerequisite: PSY-225 and two additional 200 level psychology courses.

system_requisites: Senior Psychology Majors - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: A critical exploration of topics of both historical and contemporary significance in psychology with intense interrogation of the field's diverse perspectives and methods. Prerequisite: Senior Psychology Majors. STAFF.

system_requisites: None
course_description: This course introduces Religious Studies by focusing on the key themes, historical developments, shifts, and actors that are central to the emergence and nuances of Black religious thinking in America and the African diaspora broadly. Prerequisite: None. HILLS

description_prerequisite: One 100-level "Studying Religion" course, or second-year standing
system_requisites: one 100-level "Studying Religion" course, or second-year standing - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course acquaints students with a coherent understanding of the worldview and zeitgeist of evangelical Christianity in America, with specific attention to how racial constructs and political motivations function in its contemporary iterations. Course modules will include: historical readings on the rise of evangelicalism (within the context of the 1st and 2nd Great Awakenings), religion and authoritarianism, the evangelical family and gender, religio-racial violence, and the apocalyptic themes lodged within the QAnon conspiracy. Prerequisite: One 100-level "Studying Religion" course, or second-year standing.

description_prerequisite: One 100-level "Studying Religion" course, or second-year standing
system_requisites: one 100-level "Studying Religion" course, or second-year standing - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Religious thought and religious experience are often theorized and found beyond the bounds of "established" spaces such as churches, mosques, or synagogues. This course, adopting that same mindset, privileges unconventional knowledge and mechanisms of human meaning within rap and hip-hop music and culture. While providing a grounding theorization of religion as complex human meaning-making, this course explores religious, theological, and ethical commitments in past and contemporary hip-hop music.  Prerequisite: One 100-level "Studying Religion" course, or second-year standing. HILLS

description_prerequisite: One 100-level "Studying Religion" course, HIS-100, or second-year standing
system_requisites: one 100-level "Studying Religion" course, HIS-100, or second-year standing - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Also listed as HIS-285. This course will use the work of 12th century scholar Ibn Rushd (Averroes) as a window into the theory and historical practice of Islamic law. We will cover a range of specific topics including criminal law, family law, inheritance law, and the laws of war. The class will also study how this legal system has been implemented across time, debates surrounding the questions of gender, and the contested place of religion in modern legal systems. Foreign language option available for students who do the Plus-2 option. Prerequisite: One 100-level "Studying Religion" course, HIS-100, or second-year standing. SABA

description_prerequisite: Second-year standing or one 100-level "Studying Religion" course
system_requisites: Second-year standing or one 100-level "Studying Religion" course. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: Asian Religions in the Digital Age. This course examines how Asian religions--such as Buddhism, Hinduism, Shinto, and shamanism--are practiced, represented, and transformed in a rapidly evolving digital world. We will explore online communities, religious discourse on social media, representations in visual media and video games, app-based practices, and emerging AI technologies. Through case studies and media analysis, we will engage questions of identity, commercialization, authority, and authenticity, and consider how religious life is reconfigured globally through digital technologies. Prerequisite: Second-year standing or one 100-level "Studying Religion" course.

description_prerequisite: Any 100 level course in English, Religious Studies, Anthropology, Sociology, or Peace and Conflict Studies
system_requisites: Any 100 level course in English, Religious Studies, Anthropology, Sociology, or Peace and Conflict Studies - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: Intentional Communities. Also listed as ENG-295. This course examines the theory, literature and spiritual practice of embodied collectives.  We will turn to South Asia and Africa to sympathetically explore religious, global and fictional imaginaries that offer ways of being and living beyond the limited "Enlightenment ego." Prerequisites: Any 100 level course in English, Religious Studies, Anthropology, Sociology, or Peace and Conflict Studies.

course_name: Adv Tpcs: Putting Rel Stds Wr
system_requisites: REL-311 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Putting Religious Studies to Work. This course provides an opportunity for students to reflect on their previous theoretical and methodological work over their undergraduate career by putting it into practice. Students will be responsible to plan and carry out their own advanced research project from the start to the end of the term on a topic of their own choosing. Along the way students will need to make choices about and present their individual theoretical commitments, specific methodology, professional possibilities, and how best to present themselves and their semester-long work. Class sessions will alternate between group discussions and presentations, mentored project meetings and research time. Prerequisite: REL 311.

system_requisites: None. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Introductory Special Topic: Slavic Food Stories: From Garden to Table. This seven-week short course explores Slavic food culture through literature, cookbooks, cultural histories, art, film, folklore, and memoirs. Hands-on experiences are also central to the course: students will learn to grow, prepare, and share food through activities in the Grinnell College Garden and Marcus Family Global Kitchen, developing a range of practical and analytical skills. The course examines how food reflects cultural identity, history, and the human experience while addressing hunger, food insecurity, sustainability and environmental responsibility. The class will also engage in efforts to address food insecurity and will sponsor food events for the Grinnell community. Prerequisite: None.

system_requisites: None
course_description: Also listed as General Literary Studies 291. This course examines and analyzes a number of 20th-century works in translation from several countries of Central and Eastern Europe (primarily, but not limited to the former-Yugoslavia, Poland, and the former-Czechoslovakia). Attention is devoted to how writers, artists, poets, and others attempt to understand and respond to major events and issues in specific countries, and in the region in general: war, genocide, revolution, totalitarianism, political repression, clashes of religion and culture, and quests for (self-)identity. Prerequisite: none. ARMSTRONG.

system_requisites: TUT-100 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: Empire and Its Others: Literature and Film from Central Asia and the Caucasus. Also listed as RUS-295. The Soviet Union was a country of paradoxes. While the Soviet government promoted national self-determination by establishing autonomous territories and fostering the development of national languages and cultures, it simultaneously engaged with practices of domination and control akin to European colonial empires. This course seeks to elucidate the inherent ideological tensions of the Soviet system primarily through the works of authors and filmmakers from the Caucasus and Central Asia, situating them within the broader context of what has come to be known as postcolonial theory. The Soviet Union was a country of paradoxes. This course seeks to elucidate the inherent ideological tensions of the Soviet system primarily through the works of authors and filmmakers from the Caucasus and Central Asia, situating them within the broader context of what has come to be known as postcolonial theory. Prerequisite: TUT-100.

system_requisites: TUT-100 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: BLM and Maidan: Race, Identity, Protest, and Solidarity Across Borders. What happens when we place two seemingly different social movements-Ukraine's Maidan and the Black Lives Matter movement in the United States-in conversation with one another? This seven-week discussion-based course examines questions of dignity, race, ethnicity, national identity, state violence, protest, social media, political narratives, and international solidarity through the experiences of Maidan and BLM. The course does not suggest that BLM and Maidan are equivalent. Their histories, political circumstances, and social questions are substantially different. Instead, the course asks what each movement can reveal about the other-and what comparison can teach us about justice, identity, power, and solidarity. Prerequisite: TUT-100.

system_requisites: RUS-101 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: A follow-up course to Russian 101 stressing the further study of grammatical usage and the development of speaking, reading, writing, and listening ability. Conducted in Russian. Meets three times a week; students must also sign up for two additional culture labs with our native-speaking language assistant. Prerequisite: Russian 101. STAFF.

system_requisites: RUS-102 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Conversation on free and structured themes, with topics drawn from different aspects of Russian and American life. Prerequisite: Russian 102. May be repeated once for credit when content changes. STAFF.

system_requisites: RUS-221 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: A continuation of Russian 221. Materials focus on major aspects of Russian culture, with added emphasis on the study of more complex grammatical concepts. Meets three times a week; students must also sign up for one additional culture lab with our native-speaking language assistant. Prerequisite: Russian 221. STAFF.

system_requisites: RUS-313 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Lights, Camera, Russian! Who gets to be desirable, successful, fashionable, or funny on Russian television? This advanced Russian language seminar explores contemporary Russian society and popular culture through television, from dating shows and makeover programs to reality competitions, game shows, and comedy. Working with authentic audiovisual materials, students will expand their vocabulary, develop a deeper understanding of colloquial Russian and different registers of speech, and strengthen their ability to communicate fluently and effectively in a variety of contexts. This advanced seminar will be conducted entirely in Russian. Prerequisite: Russian 313. STAFF.

system_requisites: TUT-100 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: Postcolonial African Literature in Translation. Also listed as HUM-295 and ADS-295. In this course, we will read some of the most vibrant French-language literature from the African continent in English translation, including foundational "classics" and the contemporary novels of our times, retracing some of the hopes, struggles, and issues that have marked postcolonial Africa. Away from stereotypical and incomplete images and reports, we will delve into the creative potential of fiction to help us think about memory, loss, feminism, family, migration, and more. Prerequisite: TUT-100

system_requisites: Consultation with the related course instructor and permission of the director of the science lab are required. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Individual or small group instruction emphasizing problem-solving skills. This class must be taken in conjunction with first-year sequences in physics, chemistry, or biology. Consultation with the related course instructor and permission of the director of the science lab are required. May be repeated once for credit with permission of the director. Note: Instruction is available without credit to students who cannot take the course or who need only occasional assistance. S/D/F only. MAHLAB

description_prerequisite: one year (two semesters) of biology, or chemistry, or mathematics/computer science, or physics, or psychology; and permission of the instructor
system_requisites: One year (two semesters) of biology, chemistry, mathematics/ computer science, physics, or psychology and permission of the instructor. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This discussion seminar is open to all students who have taken at least one year of science, and is encouraged for those students who are biology and chemistry student mentors, science laboratory teaching assistants, or students interested in pursuing a career in science teaching. This class will review some of the current literature in science education and focuses on examining the stages of the teaching and learning process and tools for improving teaching and learning. Prerequisite: one year (two semesters) of biology, or chemistry, or mathematics/computer science, or physics, or psychology; and permission of the instructor. MAHLAB.

system_requisites: None
catalog_notes: Description says: Second-year standing. System Requisites field says None.
course_description: Special Topic: Tuberculosis and Global Health. See ADS-295. Tuberculosis (TB) is a leading infectious disease cause of death in the world, with over 1 million deaths per year, and with the greater burden carried by sub-Saharan Africa, South and Southeast Asia. In this 7-weeks (2 cr.) course, we will explore TB's biology, epidemiology, its historical and social context both in the African global diaspora. Prerequisite: Second-year standing.

system_requisites: None
catalog_notes: Description says: Second-year standing. System Requisites field says None.
course_description: Special Topic: The Birth of American Medicine: Race and Biology. See ADS-295. In America's colonial past, the study of anatomy was intimately intertwined with the use of enslaved bodies. In this 2-cr course, we explore the social history of race and medicine and consider the contributions of Black bodies to Human Anatomy and their role in the development of American medicine. We critically interrogate the ethics and use of Black bodies in medical education. We investigate the persistence of racialized perceptions, research, and practices in clinical medicine. Prerequisite: Second-year standing.

system_requisites: None
course_description: Introduction to basic concepts, theory, and methods concerning human behavior and social structure. Special attention is paid to the scope and limitations of sociological analysis and the major empirical areas of investigation in sociology. Prerequisite: none. STAFF.

system_requisites: SOC-111 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Analysis of the causes and control of deviant behavior, e.g., alcohol and drug abuse, suicide, assault, and sexual deviance. Topics include how definitions of deviance change, how people become deviant, how deviant groups are organized, and how transactions among deviants occur. Prerequisite: Sociology 111. HAENFLER.

description_prerequisite: one 4 credit course in the social studies division
system_requisites: take one 4 credit course from the social studies division - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course undertakes a sociological study of how human behaviour, self-hood and community is shaped by and responds to algorithmic automation and robot relations. Students from all disciplines are welcome. The course is reading and writing intensive. Prerequisite: one 4 credit course in the social studies division.

description_prerequisite: Sociology 111 and at least one 200-level sociology course
system_requisites: SOC-111 and at least one 200-level sociology course. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Contemporary sociological theory considered in light of classic theories. Emphasis on the conceptual adequacy and the logical consistency of major contemporary theoretical perspectives. Prerequisite: Sociology 111 and at least one 200-level sociology course. INGLIS, HAENFLER.

description_prerequisite: Sociology 111 or Anthropology 104 and one 200-level sociology course; and Social Studies 115, Statistics 209 (preferred), or Mathematics/Statistics 336
system_requisites: SOC-111 or ANT-104 and at least one 200-level sociology course and SST-115, STA 209 (preferred), or MAT/STA-336 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Also listed as Anthropology 291. An overview of the research process in sociology and the social sciences, with emphasis on problems of epistemology, research design, techniques of sampling, methods of data collection, principles of measurement, basic methods of data analysis, and ethical considerations. This course will explore these topics through hands-on experiences including guided work on research methods through lab exercises. Prerequisite: Sociology 111 or Anthropology 104 and one 200-level sociology course; and Social Studies 115, Statistics 209 (preferred), or Mathematics/Statistics 336. QUINSAAT, PANDIAN

system_requisites: SOC-111 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: Black Politics. Beginning from the Civil War and ending with Black Lives Matter, this course explores the multifaceted ways in which African Americans have impacted both United States and Global Politics over the past 200 years. This course will elucidate the multitude of aims and perspectives that African American people have used to fight against injustice. Additionally, it will expose students to the people, social movements, organizations, and coalitions that have both made change possible and have had a cultural impact on the world. Prerequisite: SOC-111

system_requisites: SOC-111 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: The Illusion of School Choice. Cross-list EDU-295-01. Does school choice mean more educational opportunities or more competition that leaves some behind? This course offers a sociological exploration of school choice policy, examining its social, political, and cultural effects on local communities, public schools, and the broader educational landscape. Students will learn about various school choice models including charter schools, magnet programs, private and parochial institutions, homeschooling, and online education to consider their connections to issues of race, class, gender, and geography. The course traces the colonial history of public education, emphasizing the social implications of school choice policy on educational equity and social stratification. Prerequisite: SOC-111. CORREA

description_prerequisite: Third-year standing, SOC 111 and one 200-level sociology course
system_requisites: Third year standing and SOC 111 and one 200-level SOC course - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This class will investigate the global rise of right wing populist movements, the history of  fundamentalisms, and the intersection between religion and politics - both personal and public. To do so, we will interrogate the rise of Christian Nationalism in the United States,  through the lens of the sociology of religion. We will piece together the role of the "deep story," globalization, rationalization, and authoritarianism, gender, race/whiteness, aggrieved entitlement, and other conceptual tools. Prerequisite: Third-year standing, SOC 111 and one 200-level sociology course. SNOOK

description_prerequisite: One 200-level Sociology course and third year standing
system_requisites: Take at least one 200-level sociology course with grade, S, C, or better, and third-year standing. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Global Ethnography. This class explores what is innovative (theoretically, methodologically and ethically) in approaches to global ethnography; the challenges scholars face; as well as the strengths and weaknesses of global ethnography. We will discuss how sociologists and other scholars have developed new approaches to ethnography such as multi-sited fieldwork or have navigated "newer" fields such as virtual worlds. Moreover the course provides a comparative multi-disciplinary perspective on global ethnography through the examination of a range of topics such as international social movements, global religions, global media, global environmentalism, as well as migration and immigrant settlement strategies. Prerequisite: One 200-level Sociology course and third year standing.

description_prerequisite: Spanish 105 or placement by the department
system_requisites: SPN-105 or placement by the department - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course is for students who completed SPN 105 or were placed at the 106 level by the Spanish Department. Through total immersion, students will develop communicative competence in order to become active users of the Spanish language and gain confidence in speaking and interacting in real life situations. Students will gain cultural competence in the Spanish-speaking world, including the US, by reading cultural texts, researching cultural topics, and learning about Spanish-speaking peoples and their societies, histories, and cultures. Prerequisite: Spanish 105 or placement by the department. STAFF.

system_requisites: Concurrent enrollment in SPN-217 or SPN 285 - Must be taken at the same time as this course.
course_description: Work on improvement of speaking skills. Discussion and conversation based on various audiovisual cultural materials. Conducted in Spanish. Repeatable for credit. Prerequisite: Concurrent enrollment in SPN-217 or 285.

description_prerequisite: Spanish 106 wioth grade S, C, or better; or placement by department
system_requisites: SPN-106 with grade S, C, or better; or placement by department - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Development of language skills through reading, oral practice, vocabulary building, grammar review, and short compositions. Materials include short literary, nonliterary, and visual texts. Conducted in Spanish. Prerequisite: Spanish 106 wioth grade S, C, or better; or placement by department. STAFF.

system_requisites: SPN-217 or placement by department. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course will develop students' critical and interpretive commentary and analysis via literature and visual culture from Latin America, US Latinx communities, and Spain. Additionally, this course will continue to develop students' language skills both orally and in writing, as well as their cultural competency. Materials may include drama, cinema, comics, poetry, and narrative. Conducted in Spanish. Prerequisite: Spanish 217 or placement by department. STAFF.

system_requisites: SPN-217 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: Current Events in the Spanish Speaking World. This conversation-based course is designed to familiarize students with periodicals and news sources from the Spanish-speaking world as well as current events being discussed in these forums. Students will read different types of news outlets and periodicals from diverse regions of the Spanish-speaking world and study themes that are prevalent in these sources, such as politics, sports, and culture. Students will develop critical literacy skills, speaking, and writing skills, with emphasis on improvisational speaking. Prerequisite: SPN-217.

system_requisites: SPN-285 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: A study of selected, representative works from the 1920s through the 1960s. Emphasis on texts manifesting social conscience and artistic experimentation; treatment of the culture of protest and imaginative cultural expression. Consideration of poetry, narrative, and visual arts. Conducted in Spanish. Students cannot take this course after taking a seminar course in literature (SPN 377, 379, 383, 385, 386 or 395 on literature). Prerequisite: Spanish 285. APARICIO.

system_requisites: SPN-285 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Sex, Health, and Disability in the Spanish-Speaking World. This interdisciplinary course explores how people in the Spanish-speaking world have understood sexual difference, reproduction, health, and disability, from the early modern period to now. Class materials will include fiction, a graphic novel, drama, relaciones de sucesos, Inquisition documents, medical texts, articles, and more. Making comparisons across time, space, and culture, we will draw on perspectives from gender and sexuality studies, the history of medicine, and disability studies. Prerequisite: Spanish 285.

system_requisites: SPN-311, 312, 314, 315, 317 or SPN-295 on literature. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This interdisciplinary course focuses on Latinx sexualities and identities. This course will focus on literary analysis of a variety of genres and cultural texts that have served as inspiration and influence for diverse communities of Latinxs. Students will explore artistic and theoretical contributions by Latinx scholars and artists related to the construction, the performance, and the questioning of gender roles. We will study the relation between literary works and the formation and conceptualization of Latinx and Chicanx identities and communities. Finally, we will focus on artistic-intellectual interventions that reflect the heterogeneity of more contemporary Latinx and Chicanx communities, with special attention to the diversity of thought on gender and sexuality. At the end of the course, students will present their research on gender roles, power, and sexual hegemonies based on literary analysis of Latinx cultural texts. Texts will be in English, Spanish, or Spanglish. Class discussion and all written work will be in Spanish. Prerequisite: SPN-311, 312, 314, 315, 317, or SPN-295 on literature. PETRUS.

description_prerequisite: SPN-295- Constructing Identities, SPN-295 Spain Women Trvl Narratives, SPN-295 Women Detective Fiction, SPN-311, SPN-312, SPN-314, SPN-315, or SPN-317
system_requisites: SPN-295 Constructing Identities, SPN-295 Spain Women Trvl Narratives, SPN-295 Women Dectective Fiction, SPN-311, SPN-312, SPN-314, SPN-315, or SPN-317 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Advanced Special Topic: Afro Women and Religious Exemplarity. This course examines the representation of religious exemplarity of some Afro-descendant women during the 17th and 18th centuries in Spain and Latin America. The class discusses race, caste, gender, slavery, and Blackness, as well as their ideological and political functions in Spain and its colonies. The course also analyzes how some of these Afro-descendant women have become the basis of a current movement of empowerment and pride in Afro identity within digital writing spaces. Prerequisites: SPN-295- Constructing Identities, SPN-295 Spain Women Trvl Narratives, SPN-295 Women Detective Fiction, SPN-311, SPN-312, SPN-314, SPN-315, or SPN-317.

description_prerequisite: two years of high school algebra and second semester of first-year standing
system_requisites: Two years of high school algebra and second semester of first-year standing. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Introduces the notions of variability and uncertainty and such common statistical concepts as point and interval estimation and hypothesis testing. Data-oriented, with real-world examples chosen from the social and biological sciences. The computer is used for data analysis and to illustrate probabilistic and statistical concepts. Prerequisite: two years of high school algebra and second semester of first-year standing. STAFF.

description_prerequisite: TUT-100 and instructor consent Students interested in this course will need to complete an application by October 5, 2026 in addition to doing the normal registration process
system_requisites: TUT-100 and application. Open to first-year students only - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Introductory Special Topic: Totally Bananas! The Liberal Arts in a Fruit. See ANT-195. This course investigates bananas through a Liberal Arts lens. Students will examine different aspects of this fruit through the fields of Anthropology, Biology, Economics, Gender Studies, History, Literature, Political Science, and the visual and performing arts. Two themes will emerge in the course. First, bananas constitute a commodity that has shaped economic and political relationships globally. Second, bananas have varied cultural meanings- both as a food and a cultural icon. This course involves travel during spring break as well as summer 2027. Prerequisite: TUT-100 and instructor consent Students interested in this course will need to complete an application by October 5, 2026 in addition to doing the normal registration process. system_requisites: MAT-125 or 131 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: The course covers the application of basic statistical methods such as univariate graphics and summary statistics, basic statistical inference for one and two samples, linear regression (simple and multiple), one- and two-way ANOVA, and categorical data analysis. Students use statistical software to analyze data and conduct simulations. Prerequisite: Mathematics 125 or 131. STAFF.

system_requisites: STA-209. CSC-151 or computer programming experience recommended. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course introduces core topics in data science using R programming. This includes introductions to getting and cleaning data, data management, exploratory data analysis, reproducible research, and data visualization. This course incorporates case studies from multiple disciplines and emphasizes the importance of properly communicating statistical ideas. Prerequisite: STA-209. Suggested CSC-151 or computer programming experience. STAFF

system_requisites: STA 209 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course is an overview of modern approaches for building and assessing predictive models for both classification and regression tasks. Theory and implementation for common predictive techniques will be covered, including linear, penalized, and logistic regression, tree-based models, and ensemble models. Framework for model assessment, including the bias-variance trade-off, cross-validation, and resampling methods, will be discussed. This course will make extensive use of the R programming language. Prerequisite: STA-209. MILLER, WELLS

system_requisites: STA-209, or MAT/STA-336 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: In addition to a short review of hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and 1-way ANOVA, this course incorporates experiments from several disciplines to explore design and analysis techniques. Topics include factorial designs, block designs (including latin square and split plot designs), random, fixed, and mixed effects models, crossed and nested factors, contrasts, checking assumptions, and proper analysis when assumptions are not met. Prerequisite: Statistics 209, Mathematics 209, or Mathematics/Statistics 336. STAFF.

system_requisites: STA-209, STA-230, or MAT/STA-336 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course will focus on investigative statistics labs emphasizing the process of data collection and data analysis relevant for science, social science, and mathematics students. These labs will incorporate current events and interdisciplinary research, taking a problem-based approach to learn how to determine which statistical techniques are appropriate. Topics will typically include nonparametric tests, designing an experiment, and generalized linear models. Prerequisite: Statistics 209, Statistics 230, or Mathematics/Statistics 336. KUIPER.

description_prerequisite: CSC-207 and STA-230, MAT-306, or STA-310
system_requisites: CSC-207 and STA-230, MAT-306 or STA-310 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Also listed as MAT-330. Project-based course in which students work in small teams to complete the full spectrum of the data science process including developing a problem statement, data collection and processing, data analysis using an appropriate programming environment, and drawing conclusions supported by the data. Prerequisite: CSC-207 and STA-230, MAT-306, or STA-310.

system_requisites: MAT/STA-335 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Also listed as MAT-336. A systematic treatment of mathematical statistics based on probability theory. Topics will include: principles of estimation and hypothesis testing, chi-square tests, linear models including regression and analysis of variance, and nonparametric inference. A variety of applications will be considered. Prerequisite: Mathematics/Statistics 335. STAFF.

system_requisites: None
course_description: An introduction to dance technique in various styles, with a focus on the fundamentals of movement analysis. Students experience full dance classes, emphasizing the development of a physical and kinesthetic understanding of concert dance techniques. This course also examines the foundational principles, terminologies, and histories of concert dance styles. Different somatic systems and dance modalities covered will increase movement capacities of the body, help prepare students for performance, and expand creative choreographic resources. May be repeated for credit. Prerequisite: none. HURLEY.

course_name: Intro to Movement for the Perf
system_requisites: None
course_description: In this class, students develop as nuanced expressive movers and develop an understanding of their bodies as instruments of expression and communication. Working together, students build ensemble and collaboration skill as they explore creating original movement-based performance works. Trainings drawn from somatic practices, dance, physical theatre and mindfulness techniques are at the core of this course. Prerequisite: None. STAFF

system_requisites: None
course_description: Festivalizing Dance in Balinese Performing Arts. Festivals in Bali, Indonesia are not mere events of entertainment. They are confirmations of cultural bonds and processes of sustaining social relationships. Dance is integral to showcase the developments of the community while elevating discourse on any political tensions. In this class, students will learn the fundamentals of Balinese dance (tari dasar) in the contexts of festivals and artistic gatherings. Students will have a chance to learn how Balinese dance interacts with theater, popular media, and musical arts such as Gamelan. The sonorities and tactility of Balinese festivals is unique from community to community. An ideology that should be championed. This course will collaborate with the Balinese Sound Ensemble to better understand the connection of movement, music, and festivals. In the middle of the semester, students will participate in The Rocky Mountain Balinese Gamelan Festival 2027 in Denver, Colorado (an optional field trip). Then the end of the semester will culminate in a public sharing of our work and a dialogue of inter/intra-cultural dance practices. Prerequisite: None.

system_requisites: None
course_description: This course explores the multifaceted field of performance studies, including how and for whom performances are created, what cultural work they do, and what multiple meanings they may convey. Engaging in an intersectional approach to embodied and scholarly inquiry from a multiplicity of academic fields, we explore performances in order to emphasize the ways we can create critical acts that mobilize performance? theory from the perspective of our own lived experience. Prerequisite: none. STAFF.

system_requisites: None
course_description: Introductory Special Topic: Zimbabwean Dance and Ritual as Liberation Practice. See MUS-195. This three-week course offers students an immersive introduction to Zimbabwean dance as a cultural practice deeply rooted in community, history, ritual, and social change. Students will explore dance as a powerful vehicle for cultural expression, knowledge transmission, and collective transformation. Through Zimbabwean dance, music, song, and a deeper understanding of the ritual practices that accompany them, students will gain insight into Zimbabwean cultural value systems. The course emphasizes how dance reflects and shapes resistance practices. Prerequisite: None. Dates: April 26 to May 12. Short course deadlines apply.

system_requisites: THD-102 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Building on the foundations of concert dance techniques, this course combines an exploration of modern and contemporary dance genres with an emphasis on movement patterning, choreographic sequence, musicality, stylistic specificity, and individual artistry. This course is appropriate for students with previous training in dance technique. May be repeated for credit. Prerequisite: THD-102. HURLEY.

description_prerequisite: Entry into Dance Ensemble takes place at an Informational Workshop held on the second Tuesday of each semester
system_requisites: Entry into Dance Ensemble takes place at an Informational Workshop held the second Tuesday of each semester. Course registration closes at end of Add/Drop period. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Dance Ensemble is engaged in the development, rehearsal and production of dance works choreographed by faculty and guest artists. Exposure to diverse choreographic approaches provides the opportunity to expand stylistic and interpretive range. Students gain collaborative skills through improvisation and the contribution of movement material to the choreography. Dance ensemble is open to EVERY BODY. Fall semester is a Community Engaged Learning project working with a community partner. The Spring semester is a fully produced performance. May be repeated for credit. Prerequisite: Entry into Dance Ensemble takes place at an Informational Workshop held on the second Tuesday of each semester. Course registration closes at end of Add/Drop period.(A maximum of 8 practica credits may count toward graduation.) SANOU

description_prerequisite: THD 102, 110, 120, 140, ART 111, 155, MUS 110, 112, or any 200-level THD course with the exception of THD 200 or 201
system_requisites: THD 102, 110, 120, 140, ART-111, 155, MUS-100, 112 or any 200-level THD course with the exception of THD 200 and THD 201 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: This course focuses on the fundamentals and theories of choreographic processes explored through formal and experimental models and their socio-historical contexts. Improvisation and composition are used to explore the structural elements and movement vocabularies that are used to devise physical ideas for the stage that emerge as choreography and staged direction for theatrical works. Students will present their work in an end of the semester showing. Prerequisite: THD 102, 110, 120, 140, ART 111, 155, MUS 110, 112, or any 200-level THD course with the exception of THD 200 or 201. SANOU

system_requisites: THD-130 or ART-111 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: An exploration of the design fundamentals common to each facet of theatrical design: scenery, lighting, costumes, and makeup. Such elements as design procedure from conception to realization, research techniques and materials, period style, and design history are emphasized. Prerequisite: Theatre 130 or Art 111. THOMAS, HOWELL-GRITSCH

description_prerequisite: Any 100-level Theatre and Dance course except THD-100 or 101 or second-year standing
system_requisites: Any 100-level Theatre and Dance course except THD-100 or 101 or second-year standing. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Community Engaged Performance. This course introduces methodologies for interrogating and creating performance, as well as how to critique and transform the world through performance. This semester the topic centers Community-Engaged Performance, including required course-embedded travel over spring break within the US but to multiple Indigenous nations (in IA, AZ, and OK), building ethical partnerships with artists and organizations who engage with communities to address issues including environmental stewardship, refugee care, and place-based commemorative storytelling. Prerequisite: Any 100-level Theatre and Dance course except THD-100 or 101 or second-year standing. STAFF Students interested in this course will need to complete an application by October 5, 2026 in addition to doing the normal registration process. The application materials are available here: https://travel.global.grinnell.edu/_portal/. system_requisites: TUT-100 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Special Topic: Comedy Improvisation. In this 8-week short course, students will be introduced to the Upright Citizens Brigade philosophy of long form improv. Students will engage in training practices of listening, support, and commitment, practice thinking on the "top of your intelligence", and how to use audience suggestions. Students will also engage in the concepts of game, scene work, and monologue throughout the course, leading to a public imrov performance at the end of the course. Prerequisite: TUT-100

system_requisites: THD-230 or 231 - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Advanced Concert Design. Over the past quarter-century, there has been a significant change in pop music concerts, tours, and special events. The use of moving lights, projections, song-specific costumes, mobile stage pieces, and even holograms are now the expectation, creating visual spectacle on a grand scale to accompany artists' music. Bad Bunny's Super Bowl performance. Taylor Swift's Eras Tour. Beyoncé's Cowboy Carter Tour. . . All not only utilize but rely upon visual spectacle to support artists' musical messages. In this course, students will both study and engage in the process of large-scale scenography for concert design. Using 3D visualization technology, students will create virtual stage models, build lighting, projection, and audio packages, and render visual designs for musical artists. We will explore the collaborative design process between artists, technicians, engineers, and content creators to implement designs in full scale, ultimately implementing designs in one of the College's performance venues. This is an advanced course, focusing primarily on time-based media, stage lighting, and scenography. The course is constructed as an experiential, collaborative laboratory in which students will inquire, research, question, experiment, and create. Intermediate level of study in performance, design, or studio art is a required foundation for this course. Prerequisite: THD 230 or 231. THOMAS.

system_requisites: None
course_description: The Enterprise of Freelance Journalism. Journalism isn't dying, but the newsroom might be. Freelance journalists run their own enterprise by finding their own stories, setting their own hours, and working from wherever they want. This course covers the practicalities of freelancing, from identifying stories to building a platform on social media, as well as how to use those tools to build a more ethical, diverse and sustainable future for the profession. Sponsored by the Wilson Center for Innovation and Leadership. Dates: March 30 to April 29. Short course deadlines apply. Prerequisite: None.

system_requisites: None
course_description: This course will explore the phases of building a successful marketing campaign - performing research, developing a messaging strategy, creating a perfect media mix, delivering creative and analyzing success. Working in groups, students will have an opportunity to build an entire marketing campaign from scratch by selecting a faux product from a real industry. As students gain knowledge on the process, final presentations may be printed and used for portfolios. Dates: February 9 to March 2. Short course deadlines apply. Prerequisite: None.

system_requisites: Second-year standing - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Investing in Regenerative Food Systems. This five-week seminar explores how financial systems can accelerate, or impede, the transition toward regenerative food systems. It builds naturally on the fall seminar, Building Regenerative Food Systems, but is designed to stand alone. Students examine how public policy, philanthropy, lending, private investment, community finance, blended finance, and landscape finance interact with governance, partnerships, institutions, and strategy. The focus is less on technical financial modeling than on how different forms of capital can be matched and organized to support systems change. No prior background in agriculture, environmental studies, economics, or finance is required. Meets 01/27/27 to 02/24/27. Short-course deadlines apply. Prerequisite: Second-year standing.

system_requisites: None
course_description: WRT 101 introduces students to academic writing at the college level. Emphasizing writing as a process, the course provides opportunities for students to collaboratively practice writing principles in class and apply them to writing assignments in other courses through individual writing center appointments. Students must be enrolled in Tutorial or another writing intensive course to take WRT 101. Prerequisite: None. STAFF.

system_requisites: None
course_description: This course emphasizes individuality and creativity within the conventions of academic writing. Students write analytically, while infusing their work with their own personality, voice, and style. Through craft exercises and workshops, students experiment with more advanced writing techniques, like guiding metaphors and narrative vignettes, to vividly convey their ideas and engage readers. Prerequisite: None. D. PEREZ

system_requisites: None
course_description: In this course, students will approach oral communication from a writerly perspective by drafting and delivering speeches on a variety of academic topics. Special attention will be paid to audience consideration as students learn to provide effective feedback on peers' speeches. Prerequisite: none. STAFF.

system_requisites: Tutorial - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: In this course students will expand their knowledge of academic communication by analyzing academic genre conventions and English vocabulary and grammar across disciplines. The goal of the course is to make the conventions of academic communication explicit; it is intended for any student who would like to develop more confidence in reading and writing academic genres. Prerequisite: Tutorial. NICHOLS-BESEL.

description_prerequisite: New Writing Mentors have registration prioity
system_requisites: Second-year standing or completion of 200-level writing intensive course. - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
course_description: Also listed as Education 301. In this course, we will discuss theories of writing, revising, teaching, and tutoring; learn and practice strategies for effective commenting on drafts and conferencing with writers from a variety of disciplines and backgrounds; identify and investigate intriguing questions and scholarly debates related to writing, teaching, and tutoring; present the results of that research both orally and in writing; and reflect on our own experiences as writers, tutors, and learners. Prerequisite: New Writing Mentors have registration prioity. Second-year standing or completion of 200-level writing intensive course. TURK.
